title: Jimmy Rochelle's band with Milt Buckner and Wardell Gray
summary: In Michigan he joins Jimmy Rochelle, a dance band with good soloists including Milt Buckner and Wardell Gray, and compares it with Gay and Wharton.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional

blocks.x: Okay. So Step Wharton's band broke up, because there were no gigs. So I went with Jimmy Rochelle, and they had...
This was in Michigan?
Yeah.
Did you go to Michigan?
Yeah. Well, they sent for me.
Where was he? In Detroit?
No, he wasn't in Detroit.
Not yet.
In Battle Creek and Kalamazoo and places like that.
[END OF TAPE 1, SIDE 1]
Let's see, Jimmy Rochelle. Yeah, we played a lot of places, like in Battle Creek, Lansing, Kalamazoo, Grand Forks.
What kind of a band did he have?
It was pretty good. He had Milt Buckner and Wardell Gray, myself, and a cat named Duck who played trumpet...
Would you say this was the best band you had played with up to that point?
Yeah, I think it was about the best band. No, Step Wharton's band was the best band, but Jimmy's band wasn't bad, because with Milt Buckner and Wardell...
You had some good soloists.

We had some good soloists, yeah. The type of music he was playing wasn't so hot, but he had good musicians in the band. Because I used to write... Buckner used to write for the band and I'd write for the band. So we did all right as far as the music was concerned, except that he was really one of those bands that played for dancing and so forth and so on, and that's the type of jobs he had. They wasn't really nothin' outlandishly what you really dug.
Like, Leonard Gay I think was the best Swing band that I had played with up until then.
But Jimmy Rochelle had a good band. I mean, he kept working all the time, and he paid a fair wage. It wasn't nothin' to brag about, but it wasn't nothin' to cry about either.
